Theorem
[Preissman's cyclic-subgroup theorem] 1. ch12:3.2If $M$ is compact, every nontrivial abelian subgroup of $\pi _1(M)$ is infinite cyclic.
Proof

\sketch Choose a nonidentity element of the abelian subgroup $H$. By section 1, it translates along a geodesic $\tilde\gamma $. The uniqueness in item 2 and commutativity, through item 2, imply that every element of $H$ preserves $\tilde\gamma $. Now item 2 shows that $H$ is infinite cyclic.

□
